newsitem.title: USA: Cleveland Fed median CPI up 0.2 pct in November.
newsitem.headline: Cleveland Fed median CPI up 0.2 pct in November.

text.p: The Federal Reserve Bank of Cleveland said on Thursday its median Consumer Price Index rose 0.2 percent in November after a 0.3-percent increase in October.
"The median CPI rose 0.2 percent in November, or up 2.8 percent at an annualized rate," the Cleveland Fed said.
The median CPI is a core measure of inflation calculated by the Cleveland Fed based on the Bureau of Labor Statistics's monthly CPI data.
Unlike the core CPI which specifically excludes food and energy prices, the median CPI excludes any item whose price change diverges markedly from the performance of most components in the CPI index.
"Over the last 12 months, the median CPI advanced 2.9 percent, the CPI rose 3.2 percent and the CPI less food and energy climbed 2.6 percent," the Cleveland Fed said.
The median CPI also was up 2.9 percent year over year in October.
